subject: RFI: international data handling and operational safeguards (section C)
messages:
From: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@veridianhealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@veridianhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RFP — section C: international data handling and operational safeguards

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for taking this RFP. Section C of our security/privacy questionnaire focuses on international transfers, processor-processor/processor-subprocessor routing, and operational evidence for safeguards. High-level asks from our legal and procurement teams: 

1) Legal basis and mechanism for EU->US and APAC->US processing (SCCs, DPF, alternative transfer mechanisms) and whether you require additional controller-to-controller agreements.
2) A draft DPA annex or DPA annex template we can review (clauses for routing, subprocessors, audit).
3) Technical & operational controls evidence (KMS architecture, logs retention, access controls, customer tenancy/residency options).
4) A data inventory / mapping for the product features we plan to use (embedding generation + chat inference).
5) Any model-routing or fallback behavior that may route requests across regions or to model variants (how is routing controlled and audited?).

We attached the RFP excerpt (Section_C) for context. Can you confirm scope and provide the requested evidence? If it's easier, a 30–45 minute walkthrough next week would also work — procurement prefers written evidence first but legal may request a short demo.

Appreciate a target date for initial materials — our deadline for the RFP packet is Dec 20.

Best,
Sarah Connors
Sr. Manager, Vendor Risk & Privacy
Veridian Health
[Attachment: Veridian_RFP_Section_C.pdf (PDF)]

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFP — section C: international data handling and operational safeguards

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear asks and for sending the excerpt. Below is an initial package and summary; I attached the DPA annex draft and a data map CSV for the features you called out. 

Summary answers (high level):
- Transfer mechanism: For EU->US we rely on the current EU SCCs executed between controller/processor where applicable and our DPA. We also support customer-requested DPF/adequacy workflows where required by contract. When customers have residency needs we offer Dedicated and Private deployment options to avoid international egress.
- DPA annex: attached is our standard DPA Annex (dpa_annex_draft_v2.docx). It includes subprocessor list, routing policies, and an export controls exhibit.
- Technical/ops evidence: attached Runtime Export Controls Summary (runtime_export_controls_summary.pdf) and the data map (redwood_data_map_v1.csv). Highlights: KMS integration for tenant keys (optional), granular RBAC for platform ops, token-level audit logs retained 90 days by default with extended-retention add-on, and network isolation options for Private deployments.
- Model routing: policy-driven. Customers can pin region & model version. Our smart routing defaults to region-local endpoints when available; we have explicit fallbacks that are recorded in the request trace and surfaced to customers via the Console (per-request metadata). We can provide trace examples if useful.

Requested next steps / ask list: 
1) Please confirm which product features you plan to use (embedding, chat streaming, function-calling) so we can filter the data map and logs examples.
2) Legal: are you able to accept the DPA Annex in its current form, or do you need clause-level redlines back to us?
3) Procurement: if you want a short walkthrough, propose 30 minutes; Ben can lead a technical demo and Marissa can cover compliance/evidence.

Attachments included: redwood_data_map_v1.csv, dpa_annex_draft_v2.docx, runtime_export_controls_summary.pdf.

We aim to send any additional log extracts or trace samples by Dec 15 to meet your packet deadline. Let us know if that timeline works.

Regards,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Security & Compliance (Sales Engineering liaison)
Redwood Inference
[Attachments: redwood_data_map_v1.csv (CSV), dpa_annex_draft_v2.docx (DOCX), runtime_export_controls_summary.pdf (PDF)]

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Veridian packet — quick task split

Ben / Marissa — following my reply to Veridian (copied above), short action items so we align: 

Ben: can you produce a 1–2 page trace example showing a region fallback (EU -> US fallback) with request_metadata redaction? Customer asked for auditable routing. If you can include the Console trace link (sanitized) that will help. Deliverable by EOD Tue (12/14).

Marissa: legal asked whether we have any standing DPF commitments — I flagged our ability to support DPF workflows but they may request specific attestations. Please review dpa_annex_draft_v2.docx and propose any redlines for clause 5 (cross-border transfers) and clause 9 (subprocessors). Would like a short comment doc by Mon (12/13) so we can iterate before Ben sends traces.

I'll coordinate and produce the log samples (redacted) for the packet. If either of you sees anything in the runtime_export_controls_summary that needs updating please flag.

Thanks — aim to keep the RFP response tight; procurement will probably expect a combined PDF by Dec 20.

-Steph
